content:
I often work on a branch where I need to use cache that is specific to that branch. One annoyance with this is that lake exe cache get first tries to download the cache for the master branch, which downloads almost nothing (because my branch differs from master), but this step takes a lot of time (about as much time as actually downloading the master cache). Here's what that looks like:

In particular the Downloaded 1 file(s) [attempted 8149/8149 = 100%, 0 KB/s] step takes about as much time as it takes to download 8149 files.

Does anyone know if this could be fixed? cc @Marcelo Lynch

The rationale here is that we always prefer 'official' ltars (the ones pushed to the master endpoint) and there is no way to check if they exist except by probing the whole set.

In the next few weeks I'll be working on refactoring the cache tool to recognize the "developer cache" scenario in a more principled way, so this is valuable feedback, I'll keep it in mind. This case should also improve in the medium term with lake cache, which should make for a smarter resolution of the 'downloadable set'.

(One immediate way I can think of making this faster is by pivoting to iterating per-file in this chain (master, fork cache) instead of per-link-in-the-chain across the whole set of files -- but you can see for instance how this would murk the log lines that are output, etc.; in any case, I'll post any improvements on this thread!)
